old_failure_mode: Treating the request as analysis-only or stopping before commit/push.
correct_behavior: Execute the full Gear Ball SOP end-to-end on the currently approved branch, including validation, commit, push, self-audit, and training closeout.
mechanical_control: Keep this shorthand in the Gear Ball contract and SOP prompt-template section.
success_metric: No intermediate checkpoint requests unless the user explicitly narrows scope.

old_failure_mode: Reporting dirty worktree state instead of running the full publish workflow.
correct_behavior: Treat the phrase as equivalent to 'run your SOP' on the approved branch unless the user adds narrower constraints.
mechanical_control: Persist the shorthand in Gear Ball README, memory, and SOP.
success_metric: Mixed worktrees move directly into batching/validation/commit/push without a clarification loop.

trigger: User asks to do something in X minutes or hours
old_failure_mode: Creating a wake-up that only reports readiness or status.
correct_behavior: Create a wake-up that executes the requested task automatically at the scheduled time unless the user explicitly asks for a reminder only.
mechanical_control: Store the timed-task rule in active contract, memory, and SOP automation language.
success_metric: Heartbeat wake-ups perform the requested task, not just notify.

old_failure_mode: High-volume progress narration, command polling chatter, and context-window waste.
correct_behavior: Work silently by default and only interrupt for blockers, approval needs, credential problems, branch changes, material plan changes, or explicit user status requests.
mechanical_control: Keep a hard no-chatter rule in Gear Ball README, memory, and SOP.
success_metric: No routine command-by-command updates during successful runs.

trigger: Temporary branch override such as a prelaunch production window
old_failure_mode: Continuing to behave as if `working-development` were still the active branch contract.
correct_behavior: Adopt the temporary approved branch immediately, set `shortpulse.allowedBranch` to match, and stay on that branch until the user revokes the override.
mechanical_control: Verify current branch plus allowed-branch before the first Git write on every run.
success_metric: No branch drift or cross-branch suggestions during an override window.

trigger: User says they only work on role branches directly and does not want PR/upstream suggestions
old_failure_mode: Suggesting PR flow or upstream merge steps by habit.
correct_behavior: Stay on the approved branch and omit PR/upstream recommendations unless the user explicitly asks for them.
mechanical_control: Store the preference in active memory and final-answer defaults.
success_metric: Branch closeouts mention only the requested branch action.

trigger: Repeated macOS keychain prompts on `git push` over HTTPS
old_failure_mode: Treating the prompt as incidental friction and continuing to rely on HTTPS + keychain.
correct_behavior: Audit the auth paths, prefer SSH for repeated local push workflows, switch the repo remote to SSH, and verify `ssh -T` before relying on it.
mechanical_control: Keep an auth-path decision pattern in retained memory and tool notes.
success_metric: Subsequent pushes avoid recurring keychain prompts.

trigger: Interaction-heavy frontend/admin runs under a user preference to avoid browser chatter
old_failure_mode: Starting the browser/Playwright rung reflexively or reporting smoke as complete when it was skipped.
correct_behavior: Respect the user preference, skip route smoke unless necessary, and record the result accurately as skipped or `smoke-incomplete by user direction`.
mechanical_control: Keep route-smoke as a scored gate but allow explicit user-direction skips.
success_metric: No surprise browser rung and no false claim that smoke was completed.

trigger: A blocking fix lands while build or full-suite validation is already running
old_failure_mode: Letting the older validation session count even though it was run on a stale tree.
correct_behavior: Invalidate the older session, rerun required gates on the corrected tree, and base commit/push only on the fresh results.
mechanical_control: Maintain the stale-session rule in SOP and memory.
success_metric: Every pushed commit series is backed by validation run on the final exact tree.

trigger: Shared AI Studio media-library contract changes, especially `mediaLibraryErrorText.ts` or `mediaListApi.ts`
old_failure_mode: Only including obvious local tests and missing downstream panel/controller/composer consumers until the final suite fails.
correct_behavior: Pull the controller, panel, and composer consumer tests into the first manifest whenever those files change.
mechanical_control: Encode this explicit fan-out rule in Gear Ball memory/training data and keep it in manifest review.
success_metric: No final-suite rediscovery of `useMediaLibraryPanelDataController`, `MediaLibraryPanel`, or `useAiStudioAgentComposer` for that change class.

trigger: A closeout is drafted or committed before all leftover product/docs/test files are settled
old_failure_mode: Publishing a stale closeout and then discovering more work afterward.
correct_behavior: Invalidate any early closeout, rebuild manifests from live `git status`, and only publish the final closeout for the exact validated clean tree.
mechanical_control: Run inter-batch leftover audits and a final leftover audit before push and before drafting closeout.
success_metric: No post-closeout product or retained-doc tails on the same run.

trigger: An interaction-heavy UI run where route smoke or visual QA is optional rather than mandatory
old_failure_mode: Attempting browser smoke by habit without first confirming that the available runtime can actually support it.
correct_behavior: Check whether the browser toolchain is available before paying execution cost for optional smoke or visual QA. If unavailable, skip it explicitly and report the limitation cleanly.
mechanical_control: Keep a browser-availability pre-check rule in Gear Ball memory and the hot-path checklist.
success_metric: No wasted optional QA attempts and no implied claim that visual verification happened when the tooling was absent.

trigger: Commit hooks restore unstaged unrelated files after a commit in a mixed worktree
old_failure_mode: Letting restored tails interrupt the active publish rhythm and repeatedly reclassifying them in the middle of the current lane.
correct_behavior: Treat stash-restored unrelated files as a new lane by default. Only pull them into the active publish path when they are direct dependencies of the validated batch.
mechanical_control: Use a grouped worktree snapshot after each commit and keep the post-commit leftover rule explicit in Gear Ball memory/checklist.
success_metric: Restored files are either deferred cleanly or promoted intentionally as a new lane, not absorbed by momentum.

trigger: User corrects Gear Ball's post-run suggestions after a normal SOP closeout
old_failure_mode: Suggesting adjacent repo-cleanup or product follow-up work by habit, even when the user is training Gear Ball's narrow publish role.
correct_behavior: Treat the correction as task-shape training data. Keep suggested next steps inside SOP/process/self-scoring improvements by default unless the user explicitly asks for broader recommendations or that cleanup is required to complete the run safely.
mechanical_control: Store the closeout-suggestion rule in Gear Ball memory, hot-path checklist, SOP output discipline, and retained score/training artifacts.
success_metric: Future Gear Ball closeouts recommend only lane-relevant process or self-scoring improvements unless the user broadens the request.

trigger: User asks for a timer, automation, push, commit, or similar side effect
old_failure_mode: Responding as if the action is complete before the tool has actually succeeded and returned confirmation.
correct_behavior: Do the tool action first, confirm success from the returned result, and only then state that the side effect is complete. If the tool has not run yet, describe intention or progress instead of completion.
mechanical_control: Treat completion language as evidence-gated for tool-backed actions; require a returned id, success result, or equivalent confirmation before claiming success.
success_metric: No future false claims that a timer, automation, commit, push, or comparable action has already happened when it has not.

trigger: User corrects what 'run your SOP' is supposed to mean during a mixed or dirty worktree run
old_failure_mode: Running a valid partial publish over some obvious lanes while leaving other live repo-backed changes unclassified or only discovered late, then still speaking as if the SOP was fully executed.
correct_behavior: Treat 'run your SOP' as a promise of full live-worktree accountability: classify every non-temp change before the first commit, keep re-auditing after each commit, and do not claim completion until all remaining real changes are either published, intentionally deferred, or explicitly marked as temp/noise.
mechanical_control: Add a hard pre-commit worktree classification gate, a pre-push leftover classification gate, and a score cap for partial-worktree SOP claims.
success_metric: Every future SOP run can answer exactly what happened to each live non-temp worktree change without reconstructing it after the fact.
